reason: The isolation plug and shared rack controls suggest a direct way to rehearse losing Meridian's uplink.
expectation: The rack should be isolated from the external uplink while retaining its local controls.

effect: The uplink is disconnected and the door indicator remains green, but the other local paths still need testing.
reaction: The green light is reassuring, though it is not enough to establish that the system works.
reason: The offline test handset can check whether the disconnected rack still provides local service.
expectation: The handset should be able to reach the rack locally without the city feed.

effect: The radios work independently, but clinic calls still depend on the company directory for address discovery.
reaction: The missing local signpost is a surprising weakness in an otherwise working link.
reason: The local controller may be able to provide the clinic address without the company directory.

expectation: The controller will help the handset find the clinic locally.

effect: The handset now carries the local directory settings and can configure the rack through its service port.
reaction: That gives us a concrete way to replace the missing signpost.
reason: The handset can transfer the local directory settings to the disconnected rack.
expectation: The rack will be configured to find local services without Meridian's directory.

effect: The rack now runs its own service directory without the uplink; the call and water paths still need checking.
reaction: The local directory resolves the identified dependency, though it still needs a real call test.
reason: The configured handset is ready to test whether the clinic can now be reached over the radio link.
expectation: The handset should find and call the clinic using the local directory.

effect: The handset reaches Eli using the rack's local directory; the pump still needs checking during the rehearsal.
reaction: The successful call confirms the directory fix, and Eli's callback makes the test feel convincing.
reason: Ren is waiting on the clinic call for the pump check, so the local water service is the next path to test.
expectation: Ren and Eli should be able to check the water service while the clinic call remains local.

effect: The stop-and-restart test confirmed that local pump control, water flow and reporting survived the disconnected uplink; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the call and water service tested together rather than trusting the indicator alone.

mostWorthwhile.text: Finding and fixing the hidden directory dependency was the most worthwhile passage: the working radios alone did not guarantee a usable clinic call, and the later call tested the fix.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second call attempt was somewhat confusing: I chose the radio link, but the handset had to be combined with the rack instead. Automatic feedback kept it from becoming a blockage.

surprise.text: The independent radio link still relied on a company directory to find the clinic's address. That changed what I understood independence to require.

arbitrary.text: The precise partner for the call test felt a little arbitrary, although resolving the clinic name through the rack made sense once shown.

continue.text: I would continue: identifying a hidden dependency and verifying the repair through an actual call and pump test made the infrastructure problem engaging.
